newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 10.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - July 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* On Wednesday, the Dow ended down 119.88 points, or 1.51 percent, at 7,842.43 as investors took profits after the blue-chip market failed for the second straight day to punch through the 8,000-point mark.
* Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Wednesday foreign private debts were at a controllable level despite their increases.
He said the current debt-service-ratio, indicator for the ability to meet principal and interest payments, was 14.6 percent for offshore government debts and 19.6 percent for foreign private debts.

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index ended down 2.70 points, or 0.36 percent, at 738.14 after the composite index hit a record high earlier, with the impact of the economic deregulation package announced on Monday waning, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,432.00/32.50 at 0140 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,432.30/32.80.
* Small-capitalised heavy equipment distributor Intraco Penta on reports it planned to form an alliance with a U.S. firm.
* BBL Dharmala Finance on reports of a plan to issue 200 billion rupiah.
* Gajah Tunggal on reports the tyre manufacturer had told the stock exhange that it planned to supply tyres to automotive firm PT Timor Putra Nasional.
* Heavy equipment distributor United Tractors on reports it planned to announce a 300 billion rupiah rights issue.
* Property and banking stocks after the government announced measures to limit loans to the property sector.
* Food manufacturer Indofood and Mayora as sugar producers could import raw sugar, dismantling the monopoly held by state commodities regulator BULOG.
* Plantatation firms Bakrie Sumatra and London Sumtra as Indonesia has revised the export tax structure for palm oil under the latest economic deregulation package announced on Monday.
